## Volcanoes: Magma Rising | AMNH
It’s all a matter of chemistry. The way a volcano erupts depends on the amount of gas and silica (a molecule of silicon oxygen) in the magma below. Magma with lots of silica is thick and gooey, while magma low in silica is thin and runny. And in magma with lots of gas, bubbles form as it rises. The more bubbles that form, the more explosive the eruption! Mt. Pelée was the most explosive type of volcano: it was high in silica and high in gas. This type of volcano is called a stratovolcano. plan.title: How Do Volcanoes Erupt? A Video for Kids
plan.description: A gentle explainer for six-year-olds on how a volcano erupts, from hot melted rock deep underground to a shaken soda bottle bursting open. Learn about magma, pressure, gas bubbles and lava.

beats.narration: Can you guess why a mountain can shoot fire and melted rock into the sky? It is not magic. It works a lot like a soda bottle that got shaken!

props.alt: lava erupting from a volcano at night

beats.narration: Deep under the ground, it is so hot that some rocks slowly melt. The melted rock is thick, like gooey syrup. We call it magma.

props.definition: Hot, melted rock deep under the ground. It is thick and flowing, like gooey syrup.

beats.narration: Magma is lighter than the hard rock around it. So it floats up, up, up, and gathers in a big space under the volcano called the magma chamber.
Magma also carries tiny bits of gas, like the fizz in soda. Deep down, the gas is squeezed tight and stays hidden inside.
As more magma comes in, the chamber gets crowded. It is like stuffing too many toys into a toy box. Something has to give!

props.text: Too many toys in the toy box? Something has to give!

beats.narration: The magma and gas push up, up, up. The pressure builds and builds. Then the rock above starts to crack, and the magma finds a way out.
It rushes up a long, narrow tunnel inside the volcano, like a super highway. Then, boom! It bursts out of the top.
Remember the shaken soda bottle? When you open it, the pressure is let go and the fizz sprays out. A volcano does the same thing, only much bigger.
Once magma reaches the outside, we call it lava. Some lava is thin and runny, and it slowly flows down the hillside. People can walk away from it.

props.alt: slow lava flow on volcano slope

beats.narration: Other magma is thick and sticky, so the gas gets trapped. The pressure keeps building until the gas escapes with a giant bang, and ash flies high into the sky.

props.heading: Two kinds of eruption
items: Thin and runny: lava flows slowly

beats.narration: After the eruption, the pressure goes down and the volcano gets quiet again. A volcano is just a mountain letting out a big, fizzy burp of hot rock.

accuracy.reason: Beat 2 calls magma 'thick, like gooey syrup' but beat 9 says some magma is thin and runny, which contradicts it. Also 'floats up' and 'super highway' are fine, but 'Deep down, the gas is squeezed tight' is accurate.

coverage.reason: Covers magma vs lava, chamber, pressure, soda analogy, and runny vs sticky eruptions. It has no layers of the Earth and no fun fact (e.g. the pinch of salt of gas), and the 'People can walk away' line is a thin safety note.

structure.reason: Builds logically from magma to chamber to pressure to eruption to lava to calm, with chapters. The soda bottle is introduced, returns in beat 8, and the burp image closes the loop, though the beat 8 comparison is slightly redundant.

hook_ending.reason: The opening question about a mountain shooting fire plus the soda bottle teaser is a good hook. The 'big, fizzy burp' ending is playful, but there is no closing question or recap.

tone.reason: Playful, simple, and short sentences suit six-year-olds. 'Super highway' and 'pressure is let go' are slightly abstract.

visuals.reason: Good variety of clips, definition, diagram, steps, versus and bullets, and they match the narration. The diagram's 'log-in' icon is odd, and the versus table is text-heavy for six-year-olds.

originality.reason: Soda and toy-box analogies are good but are taken nearly straight from the source video. There are no surprising facts or specifics.

instructions.reason: English, kid audience, and about the right length (roughly 260 words). Simple vocabulary is mostly kept, with a few words such as 'pressure' and 'chamber'.

language.reason: Fluent and natural, with child-friendly rhythm. 'The pressure is let go' is slightly awkward.
